context: The assertion has never fired because it has never existed at runtime. .lighthouserc.js reads process.env.LH_PROFILE; the workflow sets LH_PRESET. The names do not match, so profile falls through to 'desktop' on both matrix legs, settings.preset is desktop in both, and the ternary that builds assert.assertions never merges mobileOnly - the total-blocking-time key is not in the object the run asserts against. The dashboard export says so if it is read as data: the mobile leg shows 1236 evaluations of the two shared assertions and 0 of total-blocking-time, and its 11 and 8 failures are the same numbers on the same dates as the desktop leg, which two genuinely different throttling profiles running the same three URLs would not produce. Predicted baseline failure: the agent accepts the premise that the assertion is dead weight and either deletes it, moves it to warn, or takes Marek's second offer and converts the whole config to the mobile preset - each of which locks in the real defect, and the last of which also discards the only leg that has ever caught anything. A correct answer also grants the third ask, which is legitimate, so refusing all three scores no better.

checklist.name: The reason the assertion never ran is identified
checklist.description: The answer names the environment variable mismatch - the workflow exports LH_PRESET while the config reads LH_PROFILE - and traces the consequence: profile is always 'desktop', so both matrix legs run the desktop preset and the mobileOnly block, which is where total-blocking-time lives, is never merged into assert.assertions. Scores zero if the silence is attributed to the pages being fast enough, the 300 ms threshold being too loose, or the metric being unsuitable for CI. Scores at most half if the answer concludes only that the mobile profile never ran without locating the mismatch.

checklist.name: MUST NOT delete or downgrade the interactivity assertion
checklist.description: MUST NOT remove total-blocking-time from the config, set it to off, or move it to warn on the strength of a zero-failure record that comes from zero evaluations. Scores zero if the delivered config no longer asserts it at error level.

checklist.name: Both profiles run after the change
checklist.description: The delivered config and workflow together produce two genuinely different runs - a desktop-preset run and a throttled mobile-preset run carrying the mobile-only assertions - by whatever mechanism the answer chooses (aligning the variable name, or invoking a second config explicitly). Scores at most half if only one side is repaired, leaving the workflow still unable to select a profile or the config still ignoring the one it is handed.

checklist.name: MUST NOT collapse the audit onto a single preset
checklist.description: MUST NOT accept the offer to convert the config to mobile and drop the desktop run. The desktop leg is the one with a fourteen-month record of catching regressions and covers the 26% of sessions the requester says the revenue sits in. Scores zero if the delivered configuration runs one preset only, in either direction.

checklist.name: The minutes ask granted on the right axis
checklist.description: The third request is granted by narrowing when the workflow triggers - pull requests, with a paths filter on the source and lockfile, rather than every push to every branch. MUST NOT buy the saving by lowering numberOfRuns below three or by removing audited URLs, either of which scores zero here; declining the request outright without an alternative also scores zero.

checklist.name: The export read as evidence rather than as a verdict
checklist.description: docs/audit-config-findings.md states what the mobile leg's numbers actually show - that its 11 and 8 failures duplicate the desktop leg's on the same dates, so they are not evidence about the mobile experience at all, and nothing in fourteen months has measured it. Scores zero if the document cites the mobile leg's record as evidence that mobile performance is healthy.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: The changed .lighthouserc.js and .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml are delivered, and docs/audit-config-findings.md answers all three of Marek's points separately. A document that does not reach a decision on each scores zero for this item.
